content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has clarified that the designations and presentation of material in their publications do not imply any opinion regarding the legal status of any country, territory, city, or area, nor do they address the delimitation of its frontiers or boundaries. Proprietary product names are distinguished by initial capital letters. The WHO has taken all reasonable precautions to verify the information contained in their publications. The WHO provides evidence-based recommendations on interventions to improve outcomes for preterm births. These include the use of antenatal corticosteroids (ACS) to accelerate fetal lung maturation in women at risk of preterm birth. Comparisons are made between ACS and placebo or no treatment across various subgroups, including gestational age at first dose, gestational age at birth, interval to delivery, singleton versus multiple pregnancies, preterm prelabor rupture of membranes, women with chorioamnionitis, women undergoing elective cesarean section at late preterm, women with hypertension in pregnancy, and women with growth-restricted fetuses. The efficacy of different corticosteroids and regimens, as well as repeat versus single courses of ACS, is also evaluated. Further recommendations address the use of tocolytic agents to inhibit preterm labor, including betamimetics, calcium channel blockers, cyclo-oxygenase inhibitors, magnesium sulfate, oxytocin receptor antagonists, nitric oxide donors, and progestational agents. The effectiveness of relaxin, hydration, and maintenance therapies with various agents (e.g., betamimetics, magnesium, calcium channel blockers, oxytocin antagonists) is also assessed. Magnesium sulfate is recommended for fetal neuroprotection in women at risk of preterm birth, with considerations for all women and babies, singleton and multiple pregnancies, gestational age at administration, prevention of preterm birth-related neurological complications, and retreatment scenarios. Antibiotic prophylaxis is evaluated for women at risk of preterm birth with intact membranes, as well as those with ruptured membranes. Different antibiotic regimens, including erythromycin versus co-amoxiclav and varying durations of ampicillin regimens, are compared. The mode of delivery for women at risk of preterm birth is also addressed, alongside neonatal care interventions such as kangaroo mother care (KMC) versus conventional care, continuous versus intermittent KMC, radiant warmers versus incubators, and the use of plastic bags or wraps immediately after birth for preterm newborns. For preterm newborns with respiratory distress syndrome (RDS), the WHO evaluates continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy, including early versus late initiation. Surfactant replacement therapy is assessed, comparing animal-derived surfactants, protein-free synthetic surfactants, and protein-containing synthetic surfactants. Prophylactic versus rescue surfactant therapy, with or without CPAP, and early versus late surfactant administration are also analyzed. The quality of evidence for these interventions is graded, with considerations for confidence intervals, sample sizes, and study design limitations. The WHO emphasizes the critical importance of these recommendations in improving preterm birth outcomes.
